stories.title: Marcus & Millichap Arranges Sale of Chicago Mixed-Use Property
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap arranged the sale of 5655 West Fullerton Avenue, a mixed-use property featuring 24 multifamily units and four retail suites, in the Belmont Cragin neighborhood of Chicago.“Belmont Cragin continues to attract investor interest due to its strong transportation connectivity, with convenient access to Interstate 94, the Hanson Park Metra Station and downtown Chicago,” said Sam Antreasian, director of investments. Antreasian, Ryan D. Engle, and Andrean Angelov, investment specialists in Marcus & Millichap’s Chicago Oak Brook office, had the exclusive listing to market the property on behalf of the seller and procured the buyer, both of whom were private investors.Built in 1970, the property features a mix of studio, one- and two-bedroom apartments, with 17 units renovated in the past five years, including a penthouse unit with a higher-end renovation and private outdoor deck. The 14,050-square-foot asset is located a half-mile from the Hanson Park Metra Station and approximately 10 miles from downtown Chicago. The post Marcus & Millichap Arranges Sale of Chicago Mixed-Use Property appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marcus & Millichap sold 5655 W. Fullerton, Chicago: 24 units + 4 retail in Belmont Cragin.
Belmont Cragin offers I-94 access, Metra connectivity, downtown proximity attracting investor interest.
Mixed-use small-unit deal signals continued investor appetite for neighborhood density near transit.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap arranged the sale of a 24-unit mixed-use property at 5655 West Fullerton Avenue in Chicago's Belmont Cragin neighborhood, which includes four retail suites. The broker highlighted the submarket's strong transportation connectivity, including Interstate 94 access, Hanson Park Metra Station, and convenient downtown links. The transaction reflects ongoing investor confidence in transit-oriented, mixed-use opportunities in Chicago's near-west side.
stories.impact: Belmont Cragin's continued appeal to investors signals demand for smaller-unit, transit-accessible multifamily in secondary Chicago neighborhoods. Developers should monitor this northwest corridor for ground-up development sites ahead of further transit-driven density; the Metra connection and highway access create a development window if land costs remain below the ask on secondary deals like this one.

stories.title: HPD Selects Development Team for Hunter’s Point South Parcel
stories.excerpt: A development team of Slate Property Group, The Hudson Companies and Volunteers of America­­–Greater New York was selected to build nearly 1,000 apartments on a long-vacant lot in the Hunter’s Point South neighborhood of Long Island City, Queens. To be known as The Orion, the three-building, $700-million project will designate 658 of its rental units as affordable. “Solving our affordability crisis will require creative solutions and a roll-up-your sleeves approach to create housing that works for all New Yorkers and allows them to live in dynamic, diverse, and desirable neighborhoods,” said David Schwartz, principal and co-founder of Slate Property Group. “The Orion checks all those boxes and more: it will deliver nearly a thousand new homes for New Yorkers across the income spectrum and provide essential supportive services to those who need it most, all while making Long Island City more resilient to climate change.” The project will mark the first use of the New York City Department of Housing Preservation and Development’s Mixed Income Market Initiative framework, which leverages market-rate units to help finance affordable ones. The post HPD Selects Development Team for Hunter’s Point South Parcel appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Slate, Hudson, Volunteers of America selected for ~1,000-unit Hunter's Point South, Long Island City; $700M project.
658 units affordable; uses NYC HPD's Mixed Income Market Initiative to cross-subsidize with market-rate units.
First deployment of HPD's framework signals long-term policy bet on blended income to unlock Waterfront Queens supply.
stories.summary: HPD selected a development team of Slate Property Group, The Hudson Companies, and Volunteers of America–Greater New York to build nearly 1,000 apartments on a long-vacant lot in Hunter's Point South, Queens, for $700 million. The project, called The Orion, will contain 658 affordable units and marks the first use of HPD's Mixed Income Market Initiative, which leverages market-rate rental income to finance affordable housing. The three-building development will also include climate-resilience measures.
stories.impact: Hunter's Point South and Long Island City's waterfront remain a focal point for large-scale, mixed-income multifamily development backed by public-private frameworks. The Mixed Income Market Initiative's debut signals HPD's appetite to unlock constrained Waterfront Queens sites through blended-income models; developers should track policy refinements and identify similar long-vacant parcels eligible for this subsidy structure, as it makes previously uneconomic projects feasible.

stories.title: Stotan Pursuing 345K-SF Houston Warehouse Venture
stories.excerpt: Stotan Industrial has acquired an approximately 20-acre property at 711 Rankin Road in Houston through an off-market transaction and plans to develop Stotan Crossings 45, a 345,286-square-foot Class A industrial facility. The project marks Stotan’s entry into the Houston market and expands its Texas development portfolio to approximately 1.8 million square feet. Located in the heart of Houston’s North submarket, Stotan Crossings 45 will provide seamless to Interstate 45, Hardy Toll Road, Beltway 8, and George Bush Intercontinental Airport. The development will replace an existing 40,000-square-foot building with a modern cross-dock facility featuring 68 dock positions, 47 trailer parking spaces, and 217 automobile parking spaces. Designed to accommodate logistics, distribution, and manufacturing users, Stotan Crossings 45 is expected to begin construction in the third quarter of 2026. Greg Holmes, Jason Dillee, and Savannah Smith at CBRE will oversee leasing for the project. ARCO Design/Build will serve as the project’s general contractor The post Stotan Pursuing 345K-SF Houston Warehouse Venture appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Stotan Industrial acquired 20 acres, 711 Rankin Road, Houston North submarket; 345K SF Class A warehouse planned.
Stotan Crossings 45 begins Q3 2026; expands Stotan's Texas portfolio to 1.8M SF.
Project targets logistics, distribution, manufacturing users with I-45, Hardy Toll Road, BW 8, IAH access.
stories.summary: Stotan Industrial acquired approximately 20 acres at 711 Rankin Road in Houston's North submarket and plans to develop Stotan Crossings 45, a 345,286-square-foot Class A industrial cross-dock facility. The project marks Stotan's entry into Houston and is designed to accommodate logistics, distribution, and manufacturing tenants, with construction slated to begin in Q3 2026. The facility will feature 68 dock positions and strategic proximity to multiple highway corridors and George Bush Intercontinental Airport.
stories.impact: Houston's North submarket continues to absorb large-format industrial development targeting the I-45 corridor and IAH airport cluster. Stotan's entry signals confidence in logistics demand tied to port activity and regional distribution; multifamily developers should note concurrent industrial deployment in north Houston as a corollary demand driver—warehouse jobs typically draw workforce renters to nearby submarkets, creating residential upside in northern ring areas.

stories.title: Northmarq Sources $52M in Financing for Indiana Apartments
stories.excerpt: Northmarq’s Debt and Equity team, led by Annamarie Bjorklund and Cody Field, arranged $52.15 million in debt and equity capital for Maple Knoll Apartments, a 300-unit garden-style multifamily community at 500 Bigleaf Maple Way in Westfield, Indiana. Northmarq arranged the debt and equity on behalf of the borrower, Hudson Investing, through a repeat equity partnership with Torchlight Investment and Northmarq’s direct relationship with Freddie Mac, providing a comprehensive capital solution for the acquisition. “We’re excited to continue expanding our activity in the market and helping clients like Hudson access debt, equity and investment sales solutions as they grow their portfolios,” said Bjorklund. The transaction marks Northmarq’s fourth multifamily equity raise in Indianapolis-area suburban markets. Hudson Investing plans a comprehensive renovation program at the property. Built in 2007, Maple Knoll Apartments features 18 three-story garden-style apartment buildings situated on 23.97 acres in Hamilton County. The property offers one-, two- and three-bedroom floor plans. Stay ahead of the multifamily market at Connect Apartments. bullets: Northmarq closed $52.15M debt + equity for Maple Knoll Apartments, 300 units, Westfield, Indiana.
Freddie Mac debt, Torchlight equity partnership; Hudson Investing borrower planning comprehensive renovation.
Fourth multifamily equity raise in Indianapolis suburbs signals active capital flow to secondary market acquisitions.
stories.summary: Northmarq's Debt and Equity team arranged $52.15 million in debt and equity capital for Maple Knoll Apartments, a 300-unit garden-style community in Westfield, Indiana, on behalf of borrower Hudson Investing. The transaction utilized Freddie Mac financing and a repeat equity partnership with Torchlight Investment. The property, built in 2007 and situated on 23.97 acres, will undergo comprehensive renovation; the deal marks Northmarq's fourth multifamily equity raise in the Indianapolis suburbs.
stories.impact: Indianapolis suburban markets—particularly Hamilton County—are attracting acquisition-plus-renovation capital from regional operators. The frequency of equity raises in this ring signals stabilized, renovatable assets at attractive leverage points. Developers should monitor Freddie Mac's appetite for acquisitions and value-add plays in Tier 2 Midwest markets; this capital availability may compete with ground-up development economics if acquisition cap rates compress further.

stories.title: Recycler to Open $50M Rio Grande Valley Plant
stories.excerpt: Mexican recycler Zerluma broke ground this week on a $50 million facility in the Rio Grande Valley. The 90,000-square-foot plant will rise in Mission, where it will manufacture aluminum billets for North American customers. An aluminum billet is a solid, semi-finished block or cylinder of cast aluminum used as raw feedstock for CNC machining, extrusion, or forging. The firm expects to create 70 permanent jobs and $120 million in annual economic impact. The development will be built at 300 Trinity St. Mission is just north of the Mexican border. The Rio Grande Valley has drawn numerous manufacturing investments in the last few years. In McAllen, a European automotive supplier committed to investing $225 million in a production facility. Further east, the Port of Brownsville has received billions in planned investment from autonomous shipbuilder Saronic Technologies, Elon Musk’s SpaceX, Turkish firm Karpowership and others. The post Recycler to Open $50M Rio Grande Valley Plant appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Mexican recycler Zerluma broke ground on $50M, 90K SF plant in Mission, Rio Grande Valley.
Project expected to create 70 permanent jobs, $120M annual economic impact; aluminum billet manufacturing.
Recent wave: $225M automotive supplier in McAllen, SpaceX/Saronic/Karpowership investment at Port of Brownsville.
stories.summary: Mexican recycler Zerluma broke ground on a $50 million, 90,000-square-foot aluminum billet manufacturing facility in Mission, Texas, in the Rio Grande Valley. The plant is expected to create 70 permanent jobs and generate $120 million in annual economic impact. The investment reflects a broader wave of manufacturing deployments in the Rio Grande Valley, including a $225 million automotive supplier facility in McAllen and billions in planned investment at the Port of Brownsville.
stories.impact: The Rio Grande Valley is experiencing a manufacturing and industrial surge tied to nearshoring, port investment, and cross-border supply chains. While these projects are primarily industrial/manufacturing, the aggregate job creation and capital inflow (Zerluma + automotive + SpaceX/Saronic infrastructure) will drive blue-collar and logistics-worker demand in Mission, McAllen, and Brownsville. Multifamily developers should acquire land in worker-accessible corridors near these industrial clusters, as wage growth and population in-migration will follow facility openings with a 12–24 month lag.

stories.title: CIP Real Estate Buys Broward Campus for $99M
stories.excerpt: CIP Real Estate has paid $99 million for an industrial and office park in Broward County, Fla., property records show. Called Lyons Business Park, the property includes about 10 buildings, totaling 338,000 square feet It’s located at 6601 Lyons Road in Coconut Creek, Fla., near the corner with Johnson Road, about a mile west of Florida’s Turnpike. BMO Bank, serving as an administrative agent for a group of lenders, supplied a $66.9 million acquisition loan, which is scheduled to mature in 2029. A vacant, 3,000-square-foot warehouse is currently on the market for $23 a square foot. The sellers, an entity tied to Tiffany and Lee Lasser and others, appear to have owned the 26-acre campus since the 1990s and early 2000s. The acquisition marks the second South Florida purchase for Irvine, Calif.-based CIP Real Estate in the past year, after it paid $47 million to acquire two small-bay warehouses in Hialeah from TA Realty. In 2024, the firm raised $300 million to expand its industrial footprint into the Southeast. Representatives for CIP Real Estate did not immediately respond to a request for comment, while the sellers could not be reached for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: CIP Real Estate paid $99M for Lyons Business Park, Broward County (338K SF, 10 buildings, 26 acres).
BMO Bank provided $66.9M acquisition loan maturing 2029; property near Florida Turnpike, Coconut Creek.
Second South Florida purchase for CIP in 12 months; firm raised $300M in 2024 for Southeast industrial expansion.
stories.summary: CIP Real Estate acquired Lyons Business Park in Coconut Creek, Florida, for $99 million, a 338,000-square-foot industrial and office campus spanning 10 buildings across 26 acres near Florida's Turnpike. BMO Bank supplied a $66.9 million acquisition loan due in 2029. This marks CIP's second South Florida purchase in the past year; the Irvine-based firm raised $300 million in 2024 to expand its industrial footprint into the Southeast.
stories.impact: South Florida industrial remains a capital magnet for West Coast operators seeking yield and infill land near major corridors. CIP's repeat acquisitions in Broward signal confidence in last-mile logistics demand tied to port activity and population growth. Multifamily developers should note the aggressive industrial capital deployment in Broward and Miami-Dade; sustained industrial and logistics investment implies worker demand in adjacent residential markets, supporting rental fundamentals in working-class and service-sector ring communities.

stories.title: LMXD, BedRock Secure $250M Loan for 560-Unit Astoria Housing Project
stories.excerpt: LMXD and Bedrock Real Estate Partners have closed on a $250 million loan to facilitate the purchase and construction of a housing development in Astoria, Queens, Commercial Observer has learned. The financing from New York Life Investment Management gets the wheels turning on the development of 560 mixed-income housing units at 35-10 Steinway Street, as well as a new retail location for a P.C. Richard & Son store in the neighborhood, according to the developers. “We are excited to move forward with our plan to bring mixed-income housing, including permanently affordable homes, to Steinway Street and contribute to the responsible growth of this vibrant neighborhood,” a spokesperson for LMXD and BedRock said in a statement. BedRock and LMXD acquired the site, which includes 35-18 Steinway Street, for $47.7 million last year. JLL‘s Rob Hinckley, Scott Aiese, Jeffrey Julien, Lauren Kaufman and Alex Staikos arranged the new financing for the transaction. “High-quality developments with strong sponsorship and solid fundamentals continue to attract institutional capital, and Steinway Crossing is a prime example,” Hinckley said in a statement. New York Life did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Apartment units in the Astoria project will range from studios to three-bedrooms, and 25 percent will be set aside as affordable housing for those earning 60 percent of the area median income. The building will be designed by Beyer Blinder Belle Architects & Planners with all-electric infrastructure. However, the more interesting aspect of the development is that it falls within the section of land rezoned through a 2022 Uniform Land Use Review Procedure as part of the defunct Innovation QNS project by Silverstein Properties. bullets: LMXD, BedRock closed $250M construction+acquisition loan from NY Life for 560-unit Astoria project.
35-10 Steinway Street, Queens; mixed-income units + new P.C. Richard retail; permanent affordability component.
Site acquired for $47.7M last year; JLL arranged financing; demonstrates capital availability for mixed-income Queens development.
stories.summary: LMXD and Bedrock Real Estate Partners closed a $250 million loan from New York Life Investment Management for the purchase and construction of a 560-unit mixed-income housing development at 35-10 Steinway Street in Astoria, Queens, which will also include a new P.C. Richard & Son retail location. The developers acquired the site for $47.7 million in 2023 and plan to include permanently affordable units as part of the project. JLL arranged the financing.
stories.impact: Astoria's residential pipeline continues to attract institutional construction capital and mixed-income underwriting. The $250M loan size and NY Life's participation signal strong sponsor credit and favorable project economics in Queens; this reinforces Astoria and Steinway Street as a growth corridor. Developers competing for Astoria-area sites should expect continued capital availability for mixed-income, transit-oriented projects, though land costs will reflect this competition.

stories.title: Snapchat Parent Company Subleases 199K SF From Verizon at Penn 2
stories.excerpt: Snap, the technology firm behind Snapchat, is taking over Verizon’s three-floor office lease in Manhattan’s Penn District. The 198,983-square-foot sublease spans the eighth through and 10th floors of Vornado Realty Trust’s 2 Pennsylvania Plaza, known as Penn 2, according to sources familiar with the transaction. The long-term deal, struck at a premium to Verizon’s own rent obligation, runs through 2044. It is unclear whether Snap plans to relocate from its offices at 229 West 43rd Street, where its 26,000-square-foot lease is set to expire in June 2027, or if the Penn 2 lease represents a second office. Following the sublease deal, Verizon will consolidate into its existing offices in New York City, which include a corporate headquarters at 1095 Avenue of the Americas. Cushman & Wakefield’s Josh Kuriloff, Heather Thomas, Peyton Horn and Kyle Ernest represented Verizon in the negotiations, while Snap was represented by C&W’s Ethan Silverstein, Amy Zhen and Bianca Di Mauro. C&W declined to comment on the deal. Verizon arrived at the three-floor spread in July 2025, CO previously reported, executing a 10-year lease with Vornado. A spokesperson for Vornado declined to disclose additional details on the sublease, including rent terms. Class A office asking rents in the submarket around Penn Station averaged $122.90 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to C&W data. Office sublet availability in Manhattan has contracted by more than 26 percent over the past year to its lowest level since August 2019, according to Colliers’ July market report, which first cited the sublease. Penn 2 itself is more than 90 percent leased, according to Vornado, following more than $2.5 million in upgrades to its Penn District properties. Spokespeople for Snap and Verizon did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Snap subleased 199K SF from Verizon at 2 Pennsylvania Plaza, Manhattan; floors 8–10, through 2044.
Long-term deal struck at premium to Verizon's rent; Snap may maintain or relocate from 229 W. 43rd (expires June 2027).
Verizon consolidating NYC offices; Penn 2 lease signals tech tenant demand in Penn District and office market stabilization.
stories.summary: Snap Inc. subleased 198,983 square feet of office space from Verizon across three floors (8–10) at Vornado Realty Trust's 2 Pennsylvania Plaza in Manhattan's Penn District, with a long-term deal running through 2044 at a premium to Verizon's existing rent. The transaction represents Verizon's consolidation of its NYC office footprint. It remains unclear whether Snap intends to relocate from its current 26,000-square-foot office at 229 West 43rd Street (lease expires June 2027) or operate both locations.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. The transaction reflects office market stabilization in Penn District and tech tenant appetite for large, long-term commitments; however, office leasing does not directly affect apartment DEMAND, SUPPLY, CAPITAL, or COST. Monitor Snap's ultimate consolidation decision (June 2027) for secondary signals on tech employment concentration in Manhattan, which may inform residential market positioning near major tech office hubs, but this deal is primarily an office sentiment indicator.

stories.title: Fashion House Veronica Beard Expands HQ to 60K SF at 26 West 17th Street
stories.excerpt: Apparel retail brand Veronica Beard has expanded its office headquarters to approximately 60,000 square feet at the Winter Organization’s 26 West 17th Street in Midtown South, according to landlord broker CBRE. The company, which has been in the building since about 2013, signed the new deal to renew its existing space at the building and also grow by 15,000 square feet. It will now occupy space on the second and third floors, as well as on the fifth through eighth floors of the office building two blocks west of Union Square. The asking rent and the length of the lease expansion were not disclosed. The average asking rent for office space in Midtown South was $79.41 per square foot during the second quarter of 2026, according to data from Colliers. David Stockel and Taylor Walker from CBRE represented ownership in the deal. “Veronica Beard’s decision to renew and expand its footprint at 26 West 17th Street demonstrates confidence in both the location and its future growth trajectory,” Stockel said in a statement. “The transaction highlights continued demand from established tenants for high-quality office environments that support collaboration, culture and business expansion.” JLL’s TJ Hochanadel and Robert Martin handled things on behalf of Veronica Beard. “Veronica Beard has grown its business at 26 West 17th Street since establishing its first office there,” Martin told Commercial Observer. “We aligned their real estate strategy with their business trajectory, and as they continued scaling, a more sustainable long-term solution became necessary.” Veronica Beard is led by sisters-in-law Veronica Miele Beard and Veronica Swanson Beard. The brand has retail stores in New York at 41 Grand Street in SoHo and 988 Madison Avenue on the Upper East Side. Built in 1907, 26 West 17th Street is a 12-story office building with tenants including wholesale marketplace Faire and energy equipment and solutions provider Scale Microgrids.
bullets: Veronica Beard expanded HQ to 60K SF at 26 W. 17th Street, Midtown South; renewed + grew by 15K SF.
Occupies floors 2–3 and 5–8; in building since ~2013; Winter Organization ownership.
Midtown South avg. asking rent Q2 2026: $79.41/SF; apparel brand expansion signals tenant confidence in submarket.
stories.summary: Fashion brand Veronica Beard expanded its office headquarters to approximately 60,000 square feet at 26 West 17th Street in Midtown South, renewing its existing space and growing by 15,000 square feet. The company, which has occupied the Winter Organization-owned building since around 2013, will now span floors 2–3 and 5–8. The average asking rent for office space in Midtown South stood at $79.41 per square foot in Q2 2026.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. The renewal and expansion reflect office tenant confidence in Midtown South's retail and workplace ecosystems, but office leasing activity does not drive apartment DEMAND, SUPPLY, CAPITAL, or COST. Multifamily developers should note only that stable, profitable apparel companies expanding HQ footprints may support adjacent residential demand through employee density and wage growth, but this is a weak secondary signal.

stories.title: PCCP, Integrity Community Builders Form BTR Programmatic JV
stories.excerpt: Integrity Community Builders (ICB) and PCCP have formed a programmatic joint venture to develop build-to-rent (BTR) communities across the U.S., Commercial Observer can first report. The new JV will marry Houston-based ICB’s experience in land acquisition, development and construction with PCCP’s institutional investment expertise. As co-investors, the partners will deploy up to $200 million per year into BTR communities — comprising detached homes, townhomes and cottage-style rentals — in the markets ICB and its affiliates currently operate in. “We believe this venture allows us to scale our build-to-rent platform with the right asset-managing partner,” Chad Durham, vice president of BTR at ICB, said in a statement. “Together with PCCP, our goal is creating thoughtfully designed rental communities in up to 19 markets.” Jennifer Diaz, partner and head of multifamily for PCCP, said the partnership reflects a strategic focus for PCCP: expansion into BTR. “We are proud to partner with ICB as we seek to develop high-quality build-to-rent communities in growth markets,” she said in a statement. Integrity Community Builders, a wholly owned subsidiary of Weekly Homes, was founded in 2020, and has since built 22 communities with another five under construction for a total of 3,000 rental homes. The firm has worked with PCCP in the past as a general contractor, having built several communities for PCCP. “We feel like we’ve developed a pretty good brand and reputation in the space as a general contractor, serving clients like PCCP and other sponsors,” Durham said. “We knew that we wouldn’t be able to control our growth and get to the number of homes per year that we’d like to be building — which is 1,500, plus or minus — by just depending on other sponsors bringing us projects to build, or going into the market and trying to find sponsors on projects that we’ve sourced. So strategically, we always liked the idea of doing what we’ve done here with
bullets: PCCP, Integrity Community Builders formed $200M/year BTR programmatic JV across up to 19 U.S. markets.
ICB provides land acquisition, development, construction; PCCP contributes institutional capital and asset management.
Partnership targets detached homes, townhomes, cottage-style rentals in ICB's existing market footprint (Houston-based operator).
stories.summary: Integrity Community Builders (ICB) and PCCP announced a programmatic joint venture to develop build-to-rent communities nationwide, with plans to deploy up to $200 million per year into BTR communities comprising detached homes, townhomes, and cottage-style rentals. The JV will operate in up to 19 markets where ICB and its affiliates currently have presence, leveraging ICB's land acquisition, development, and construction expertise with PCCP's institutional investment and asset management capabilities.
stories.impact: This JV signals accelerating capital deployment into single-family and low-rise BTR across mid-sized and secondary markets, likely including Texas, the Southeast, and Sunbelt regions where ICB operates. The $200M annual deployment rate and 19-market scope indicate BTR is maturing from niche to programmatic asset class, competing directly with garden-style apartment development for land and labor in Sunbelt submarkets. Multifamily developers should expect increased land competition and construction cost pressure in ICB's footprint as BTR capital scales; conversely, BTR's success in these markets may validate demand, supporting multifamily fundamentals in adjacent markets.
